properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 2:06PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Hardin,
Orange, Jefferson and Jasper Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Major flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon CDT.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Water begins to go over Bigner Road into the
saltwater barrier. Water also cuts off most access to the Four Oaks
Ranch Road downstream of Four Oaks boat launch. Flooding of
Colliers Ferry Park and secondary roads near the river can be
expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight and continue rising to a crest of 6.9 feet Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 10:35AM CDT until September 3 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Long King Creek near Livingston affecting Polk and San Jacinto
Counties.

For the Long King Creek...including Livingston...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Long King Creek near Livingston.

* WHEN...From this morning to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 19.0 feet, At levels above 19 feet, minor lowland
flooding begins as water escapes the main channel of the creek. At
25.0 feet, At levels above 25 feet, moderate lowland flooding
begins as low-lying areas along the creek become inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday was 19.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 23.1 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 23.2
feet on 07/27/2024.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 445 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 2 at 1:28PM MST until September 2 at 4:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 430 PM MST.

* At 128 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area,
especially with  thunderstorms near Sierrita mine west of Green
Valley. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sahuarita, Green Valley and East Sahuarita.

This includes Interstate 19 between mile markers 38 and 47.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 2 at 5:02PM EDT until September 2 at 5:30PM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
SVRLWX

The National Weather Service in Sterling Virginia has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
East central Albemarle County in central Virginia...

* Until 530 PM EDT.

* At 502 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Boswells Tavern to near Lake Monticello, moving
south at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damaging winds will cause some trees and large branches
to fall. This could injure those outdoors, as well as
damage homes and vehicles. Roadways may become blocked by
downed trees. Localized power outages are possible.
Unsecured light objects may become projectiles.

* Locations impacted include...
Campbell, Boyd Tavern, Cobham, Keswick, Cismont, and Shadwell.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 12:24PM CDT until September 2 at 9:30PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Hardin County in southeastern Texas...
Central Jasper County in southeastern Texas...
Northwestern Jefferson County in southeastern Texas...
Tyler County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to Heavy rainfall has occurred last night and this
morning. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 4 and 20 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Woodville, Kountze, Sour Lake, Colmesneil,
Chester, Warren, Wildwood, Fred, Thicket, Saratoga, Town Bluff,
Rockland, Bevil Oaks, Village Mills, Honey Island, Caney Head and
Spurger.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:

limits, and has exited the warned area. Therefore, the warning will
be allowed to expire.  However, heavy rain is still possible with
this thunderstorm.
